Units: Count Valid dimensions: * Source ARN * Flow ARN * Availability Zone * All flows |\\\\n| `SourceARQRequests` | The number of retransmitted packets that were requested through automatic repeat request (ARQ) and received. This metric applies to sources that use the RIST, Zixi, or SRT protocol. It doesn\\'t apply to flows that receive content from an entitlement. Units: Count Valid dimensions: * Source ARN * Flow ARN * Availability Zone * All flows |\\\\n| `SourceBitRate` | The bitrate of the incoming (source) video. Units: bits per second (bps) Valid dimensions: * Source ARN * Flow ARN * Availability Zone * All flows **Note:** Both MediaConnect and the Zixi protocol use bandwidth optimization techniques that can affect bitrate measurements: * In flows with Zixi sources, Zixi often optimizes network usage by substituting repetitive content packets with null packets. * For entitlements, MediaConnect performs similar optimization between the content originator\\'s flow and the subscriber\\'s flow. For example, in a 30 Mbps stream with repetitive content (like a black slate), either optimization might reduce the bitrate to 5 Mbps. These bitrate fluctuations are normal and don\\'t affect content quality, but they might be noticeable in your bitrate monitoring. We recommend that you monitor source health as a combination of `SourceBitRate` and other metrics such as `SourceContinuityCounter` and `SourceNotRecoveredPackets`. |\\\\n| `SourceConnected` | The status of the source. A value of 1 indicates that the source is connected and a value of 0 (zero) indicates that the source is disconnected. This metric applies only to sources that use the Zixi or SRT protocol. The Max Bitrate needs an acceptable overhead established for a working buffer, for instances when packets arrive at the same time. This can lead to the wrong source showing in the output and incorrect metrics due to parsing multiple sets of incoming packets\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/media/troubleshooting-srt-and-zixi-with-aws-elemental-mediaconnect/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How to set up a resilient end-to-end live workflow using AWS Elemental products and services: Part 4 | AWS for M&E Blog\",\"context\":\"### Resilient input and transport with AWS Elemental MediaConnect\\\\n\\\\nAWS Elemental MediaConnect is a reliable, secure, and flexible transport service for live video that enables broadcasters and content owners to build live video workflows and securely share live content with partners and customers.\\\\n\\\\nMediaConnect supports redundant inputs and outputs, ensuring resiliency using primary and secondary flows as described in part two of this blog series. The SMPTE-2022-7 standard (seamless protection switching at the packet level) is used if the two sources are compliant; otherwise, active/active failover is used.\\\\n\\\\n[](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/fb644351560d8296fe6da332236b1f8d61b2828a/2020/12/16/failover.gif)\\\\n\\\\nAutomatic source failover is a setup that involves two redundant sources for a flow. {"id": "3a90f0b8-3ca2-49b6-b5c6-77d54cb16c8c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "## Pattern: encoder/upstream issue, not network transport loss

What you're describing — `SourceBitRate` dipping briefly while `PCR` errors and `SourceContinuityCounter` errors appear, but `SourceConnected` stays at `1` and `SourceDisconnections` stays at `0` — is consistent with a **transport-stream integrity problem originating upstream of (or at) the encoder/Link device itself**, not a loss of network connectivity to MediaConnect.

A few things point that way:
- **PCR errors** indicate clock/timing discontinuities in the transport stream — often from encoder-side issues (e.g. the Link device's internal encoding, bonding/cellular modem hiccups, or source video instability) rather than packet loss in transit.
- **Continuity counter errors** mean packets are arriving out of sequence or being dropped *within the stream itself*, which can happen even when the underlying connection to MediaConnect never drops.
- AWS's own guidance on `SourceBitRate` specifically warns that bitrate fluctuations can occur for legitimate reasons (bandwidth optimization, repetitive/static content being null-packet-substituted) and recommends **not** reading bitrate dips alone as a health signal — you have to combine it with `SourceContinuityCounter` and `SourceNotRecoveredPackets` to get the real picture.

## The metric that separates this from network loss

**`SourceConnected`** (and its companion `SourceDisconnections`) is the deciding signal. If the flow had actually lost network connectivity to MediaConnect, you'd expect `SourceConnected` to drop to `0` and `SourceDisconnections` to increment. Since both stay flat, the transport-level connection to MediaConnect never dropped — the Link device/source stayed connected throughout. That isolates the problem to stream content/encoding integrity (PCR/continuity counter errors riding on top of a stable connection) rather than a network outage or disconnection event.

If you want, I can pull the actual CloudWatch metrics for a specific flow/source to confirm this pattern is what's happening in your environment — just point me at the flow ARN.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
